a proven ability to define how complex opportunities are approached and won</li> <li>Outstanding writing and storytelling ability, with experience leading narrative development for high-value, multi-disciplinary pitches</li> <li>Strong commercial acumen, with experience designing and influencing commercial models, pricing strategies and value propositions</li> <li>Able to use and apply AI credible communicator, with experience presenting to senior clients and influencing at leadership level</li> <li>Comfortable operating at pace and under pressure, managing multiple high-stakes opportunities simultaneously</li> <li>Strong understanding of integrated marketing ecosystems, including the intersection of media, creative and production</li> <li>Able to influence and align senior title: HR Technology Director
description: <p><strong>About the role</strong></p> <p>The Director, HR Technology &amp; Solutions Delivery is a senior technology leadership role responsible for the strategy, design, delivery, operation and evolution of Inizio's global HR technology ecosystem.</p> <p>In the near term, the role has significant accountability for Workday, leading day-to-day IT operations, functional solution design, enhancements, continuous improvement and strategic HR technology projects.</p> <p>Over time, the role will evolve HR Technology towards a stronger platform engineering and architecture-led model, establishing the technical strategy, engineering practices, integration architecture, governance, security and operational capabilities required to support Inizio at scale.</p> <p>This requires a leader who can operate across both the functional and technical dimensions of Workday – translating HR requirements into effective solutions while bringing the technical depth and engineering mindset to shape the future HR technology landscape.</p> <p>You will have end-to-end IT accountability for Workday and the wider HR technology ecosystem. The Workday IT Operations team will report directly to this role, which reports to the Deputy Chief Information Officer.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <p><strong>Workday Platform, Operations &amp; Functional Design</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide end-to-end IT ownership of Workday, covering functional design, configuration, operations, support, enhancements and continuous improvement.</li> <li>Partner with HR People Services and Centres of Excellence to translate business requirements into scalable, sustainable Workday solutions aligned with global standards.</li> <li>Provide senior oversight of Workday business processes, configuration, security, reporting, integrations and adoption of new platform capabilities.</li> <li>Lead the Workday IT Operations team, ensuring effective management of incidents, requests, defects, changes, enhancements and releases.</li> <li>Establish effective service levels, operational KPIs, demand and backlog management, root-cause analysis, testing, documentation and operational controls.</li> <li>Drive continuous improvement, automation and proactive platform management to improve user experience, reliability and operational efficiency.</li> <li>Act as the senior escalation and decision point for significant Workday functional, technical and operational matters.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>HR Technology Project &amp; Solutions Delivery</strong></p> <ul> <li>HR Technology Strategy: Own end-to-end technology delivery of significant Workday and wider HR technology initiatives, from requirements and solution design through build, integration, testing, deployment, stabilisation and BAU transition.</li> <li>Lead Workday enhancements, module implementations, optimisation initiatives and HR transformation projects.</li> <li>Ensure solutions align with business outcomes, architecture principles and the longer-term HR technology roadmap.</li> <li>Establish delivery governance across scope, plans, dependencies, resources, risks, quality and budget.</li> <li>Hold systems integrators and delivery partners accountable for delivery, solution quality, knowledge transfer and sustainable support.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Architecture &amp; Engineering</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define the technology strategy, target architecture and multi-year roadmap for Inizio's global HR technology ecosystem.</li> <li>Establish architecture and engineering principles across platforms, integrations, APIs, data, identity, security, environments, testing, deployment, monitoring and operational resilience.</li> <li>Lead the progressive evolution of HR Technology towards a stronger platform engineering operating model, increasing automation, standardisation and engineering discipline.</li> <li>Ensure HR technology is scalable, secure, resilient, maintainable and aligned with Inizio's wider enterprise technology strategy.</li> <li>Manage technical debt and identify opportunities to simplify and modernise the HR technology estate.</li> <li>Develop internal technical capability and reduce unnecessary reliance on external partners for core platform knowledge.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Integrations, Security &amp; Technical Governance</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own technical governance across HR technology architecture, integrations, security and change.</li> <li>Ensure secure and reliable connectivity between Workday, HR applications, enterprise platforms, identity services, data platforms and external providers.</li> <li>Establish appropriate integration patterns, APIs, middleware and data standards, reducing unnecessary point-to-point connectivity.</li> <li>Ensure appropriate controls across cyber security, data privacy, identity and access management, privileged access, segregation of duties and change management.</li> <li>Embed security, risk and compliance requirements into solution design and delivery and maintain appropriate controls and audit evidence.</li> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Data and Integration teams to ensure HR technology aligns with enterprise standards.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Vendor, Commercial &amp; HR Partnership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as the senior IT partner to HR leadership, translating HR strategy and operational priorities into an actionable technology roadmap.</li> <li>Work with HR People Services and Centres of Excellence to shape solutions and prioritise BAU enhancements, projects and strategic investments.</li> <li>Provide guidance on Workday capabilities and wider opportunities including automation, AI and emerging HR technologies.</li> <li>Manage strategic relationships with Workday, technology vendors, systems integrators and specialist partners.</li> <li>Hold partners accountable for technical capability, solution quality, service, delivery and commercial outcomes and provide technology leadership for vendor selection and investment decisions.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Leadership &amp; Capability Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build and lead a high-performing HR Technology team with the right balance of Workday functional, technical, integration, engineering and operational capabilities.</li> <li>Develop the technical maturity of the function through coaching, standards and strong engineering practices.</li> <li>Foster collaboration across HR, Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Data, Integration and wider IT.</li> <li>Establish a culture of ownership, customer focus, engineering quality, accountability and continuous improvement.</li> <li>Act as a visible and credible senior technology leader across the organisation.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>About you</strong></p> <p>You are an experienced HR technology leader who combines strong Workday functional and delivery expertise with technical depth and an engineering mindset.</p> <p>You understand how Workday supports end-to-end HR processes and can lead functional solution design and delivery, while being equally comfortable discussing integrations, architecture, security, engineering and enterprise technology.</p> <p>You will bring:</p> <ul> <li>Significant experience leading Workday in a complex enterprise environment across functional design, BAU operations, enhancements and project delivery.</li> <li>Strong Workday functional solution-design expertise across multiple areas, with an understanding of HCM processes, configuration, security, reporting, integrations and data.</li> <li>Proven experience delivering significant Workday implementations, module deployments, transformations or optimisation programmes.</li> <li>Strong understanding of enterprise integrations, APIs, middleware, data integration and connectivity.</li> <li>Understanding of platform engineering practices including testing, deployment, monitoring, automation and operational resilience.</li> <li>Strong understanding of application security, identity and access management, technology risk, data privacy and change controls.</li> <li>Experience establishing effective technical and functional governance for enterprise applications.</li> <li>Demonstrated success managing systems integrators, vendors and strategic partners.</li> <li>Experience building and leading multidisciplinary technology teams.</li> <li>Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across HR and Technology leadership.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Critically, you will be comfortable operating across the full spectrum from Workday functional design and day-to-day platform decisions through to enterprise architecture and technology strategy.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Desirable</p> <ul> <li>Senior Manager, Director or equivalent experience within a global organisation.</li> <li>Deep experience across Workday HCM and multiple Workday modules, supported by Workday certifications and/or demonstrable functional and technical expertise.</li> <li>Experience leading global Workday deployments, optimisation programmes or major HR transformations.</li> <li>Experience within consulting, technology, pharmaceutical, life sciences or another complex multinational environment.</li> <li>Experience introducing platform engineering, DevOps, automation or product-oriented ways of working into enterprise applications.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>About Inizio</strong></p> <p>At Inizio, we're a global team motivated by a shared purpose: to reimagine health.</p> <p>Formed in 2022, we unite decades of experience and expertise with data, technology, and AI to create tailored solutions that drive Intelligent Commercialization™ at every stage of the journey - from discovery to post-launch.</p> <p>Our global network of over 10,000 experts operates across 50 countries, supporting clients with strategic insight, medical excellence, creative engagement, and real-world delivery. We work with the world's leading health and life sciences businesses to solve complex challenges and accomplish meaningful outcomes for our clients and patients.</p> <p>What sets Inizio apart is our people - and we believe everyone should excel. Here, you're encouraged to reimagine your possibilities: to grow, to be curious and to make change happen. We value your individuality, support your development, and celebrate your ambition. If you're ready to push boundaries and accelerate your career, Inizio is the best place to be.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Our Pledge</strong></p> <p>At Inizio, we value inclusivity, recognize the power of diversity and inspire the next generation of change-makers. We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe in creating a dynamic work environment that values diversity, equity and inclusion. We aim to recruit from a diverse slate of candidates and foster an environment that provides the right conditions for long-term success. We welcome all applications. We consider them regardless of race, color, religion, or belief. We also consider them regardless of gender, gender identity, age, national origin, marital status, military veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, and physical or mental disability.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Artificial Intelligence</strong></p> <p>Inizio may use AI technologies to support certain aspects of our recruitment process, but all hiring decisions at Inizio are made by our human recruiting team. We are committed to fair, inclusive, and human-led hiring practices.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>#LI-DT2 #LI-HYBRID</p><div class="content-conclusion"><div class="elementToProof"><em>Don't meet every job requirement? That's okay! Our company is dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role, but your experience doesn't perfectly fit every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this role or others.</em></div></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: <div class="content-intro"><p></p> <p><strong><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">About THG Ingenuity</span></strong></p> <p>THG Ingenuity is a fully integrated digital commerce ecosystem, designed to power brands without limits. Our global end-to-end tech platform is comprised of three products: THG Commerce, THG Studios, THG Fulfilment.&nbsp;</p> <p>Each represents a single, unified solution, overcoming challenges and taking brands direct-to-consumer. Our client portfolio includes globally recognised brands such as Coca-Cola, Nestle, Elemis, Homebase, and Proctor &amp; Gamble.</p></div><p>Team:&nbsp;Search &amp; Social (Commerce Division), THG Ingenuity</p> <p><strong>Introduction</strong></p> <p>THG Ingenuity is a leading ecommerce and technology business, powering some of the world's most recognised brands. Our Search &amp; Social team sits within the wider Commerce division, operating at the intersection of ecommerce, marketing, and commercial strategy. Alongside our Content and Paid Media teams, we connect brands with customers through world-class organic and paid search strategies.</p> <p>We're looking for an ambitious, detail-oriented graduate to join our team and help shape the future of search. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a passion for SEO to build a career at the forefront of digital marketing, working on Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and AI-driven search within a fast-paced, high-growth environment.</p> <p>Success in this role requires a deep curiosity for search engine algorithms, strong analytical skills, commercial awareness, and the ability to build positive relationships with internal teams (like eCommerce, Paid Media, and project management) and external brand clients.</p> <p><strong>The Role</strong></p> <p>As an SEO &amp; GEO Executive, you will support the planning, execution, optimisation, and reporting of organic search campaigns across multiple brands. You will work to grow organic visibility, traffic, and revenue, ensuring our clients dominate the search engine results pages (SERPs).</p> <p>You'll work in close partnership with our Paid Media team to ensure our organic and paid search strategies are fully aligned. You'll also collaborate daily with the eCommerce teams who are trading the sites, project teams managing site onboards, and external brand partners, ensuring SEO is a core pillar of our commercial success.</p> <p>This role combines technical SEO, content strategy, performance analysis, and stakeholder management, providing a well-rounded foundation in the future of search.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support the end-to-end delivery of SEO strategies for multiple brands.</li> <li>Conduct keyword research, content gap analysis, and SERP analysis to identify new growth opportunities.</li> <li>Perform technical SEO audits to identify and fix issues related to site architecture, crawlability, and indexation.</li> <li>Collaborate with content teams to ensure on-page content is optimised for both users and search engines.</li> <li>Analyse and report on organic performance using Google Search Console, GA4, and industry-standard search analytics platforms.</li> <li>Work closely with the Paid Media team to share search query insights, coordinate keyword targeting, and develop a unified search strategy.</li> <li>Support project teams with SEO requirements for site migrations and new client onboards.</li> <li>Stay informed on algorithm updates, competitor activity, and emerging trends, particularly in AI-driven search and GEO.</li> <li>Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders (eCommerce, Content, Paid Media) and external brand clients.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About You</strong></p> <p>We're looking for someone who is:</p> <ul> <li>A recent graduate with a primary passion for SEO and organic search, and a keen interest in related fields like Paid Media, eCommerce, client services, or digital marketing.</li> <li>Highly organised with strong time management and prioritisation skills.</li> <li>Detail-oriented with exceptionally high standards of accuracy and quality.</li> <li>Commercially aware and interested in how SEO drives business performance.</li> <li>A strong communicator with excellent written and verbal communication skills.</li> <li>Professional, collaborative and able to build positive stakeholder relationships with both internal teams and external clients.</li> <li>Proactive, accountable and comfortable taking ownership of their work.</li> <li>Curious, adaptable and eager to learn about the future of search.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills &amp; Experience</strong></p> <p>Essential</p> <ul> <li>A foundational understanding of SEO principles (technical, on-page, and off-page).</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.</li> <li>Excellent attention to detail.</li> <li>Strong written communication skills, including grammar and spelling.</li> <li>Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.</li> <li>Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively.</li> <li>A genuine appetite and eagerness to learn and develop.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable</strong></p> <ul> <li>Some hands-on experience with Google Search Console and Google Analytics (GA4).</li> <li>Familiarity with web crawling or search analytics platforms.</li> <li>Understanding of the relationship between SEO and other digital marketing channels like Paid Media, Content, and eCommerce.</li> <li>Experience working in a fast-paced, commercial environment.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>THG Ingenuity is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you are invited to interview, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to the recruitment process that will enable you to perform to the best of your ability.</strong></p> <p><strong>THG Ingenuity is committed to creating a diverse &amp; inclusive environment and hence welcomes applications from all sections of the community.</strong></p> <p><strong>Because of the high volumes of applications our opportunities attract, it sometimes takes us time to review and consider them all. We endeavour to respond to every application we receive within 14 days. If you haven't heard from us within that time frame or should you have any specific questions about this or other applications for positions at THG Ingenuity please contact one of our <span class="mark75xs2u5gf" data-markjs="true" data-ogac="" data-ogab="" data-ogsc="" data-ogsb="">Talent</span> team to discuss further.</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Fullstack Engineer, Consumer Order Experience
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Why Deliveroo? We're building the definitive online food company, transforming the way the world eats by making hyper-local food more convenient and accessible. We're at the forefront of an industry, powered by our market-leading technology and unrivalled network to bring incredible convenience and selection to our customers. Working at Deliveroo is the perfect environment to build a definitive career, motivated by impact on your own development, on Deliveroo as we scale, and on the marketplace and communities we serve. Consumer Ordering Experience owns the core purchase journey: the store page, item page, basket, and checkout flow, across both app and web. title: Electrical Engineer II (Integrations)
description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. 🐙 Kraken Generation Flex The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid. Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets. 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing. You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset. Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing. 🚀 What you'll own Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members. Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team. Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on. Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time. Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers. Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team. Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows. Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites. 🧠 What you'll bring to the party Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets. Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process. Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution. Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation. Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control. Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation. Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support. Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus. CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion. Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team. Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them. Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration. A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time. Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote. ⭐️ Bonus points Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in. Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures. Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows. Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness). Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations. Are you ready for a career with us? We want to ensure you have the right tools and environment to unleash your potential. If you have any accommodation requests, please contact us at ----- We’ll do our best to tailor the experience to your needs so you can feel comfortable, confident and be at your best! Whoever you are, if you like one of our jobs, we encourage you to apply as you might just be the candidate we’re looking for! At Kraken, we're creating a team of genuine, honest, empathetic people. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

  • Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness).

  • Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations.

title: Head of Engineering - Optimisation & Control
description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. 🏡 Where you'll fit in: KrakenFlex is the flexibility arm of the Kraken group, built to put a big green dent in global carbon emissions by rewriting how electricity grids operate. We stabilize the grid and help renewables come online much faster by managing the second-by-second balance of clean power. Right now, our platform connects nearly one million assets worldwide, putting over 6GW of live load under our direct control. Behind the scenes, that means handling massive technical scale: solving complex optimization problems in real time and processing 15 billion data readings a day from the latest green technologies, ensuring the grid stays reliable without relying on old fossil-fuel backup plants. The next phase of our journey involves monumental growth. Currently operational across multiple countries, we are poised for further global expansion, scaling our asset base and tackling unique grid challenges in new territories. Our mission is to integrate an increasingly diverse array of green flexibility assets while ensuring our market-leading platform remains exceptionally stable and performant. What is Optimisation in Flex? The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns. The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies. The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute. Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine. 🚀 What you’ll own: The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). A Head of Engineering leading a Chapter is a senior leadership role combining strong product thinking, engineering judgement, operational awareness, and people leadership. They manage managers and senior individual contributors, helping teams own their product surfaces, make sound trade-offs, and deliver reliably. This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. raw.title: Head of Engineering - Optimisation & Control
raw.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in:
KrakenFlex is the flexibility arm of the Kraken group, built to put a big green dent in global carbon emissions by rewriting how electricity grids operate. We stabilize the grid and help renewables come online much faster by managing the second-by-second balance of clean power. Right now, our platform connects nearly one million assets worldwide, putting over 6GW of live load under our direct control.

Behind the scenes, that means handling massive technical scale: solving complex optimization problems in real time and processing 15 billion data readings a day from the latest green technologies, ensuring the grid stays reliable without relying on old fossil-fuel backup plants.

The next phase of our journey involves monumental growth. Currently operational across multiple countries, we are poised for further global expansion, scaling our asset base and tackling unique grid challenges in new territories. Our mission is to integrate an increasingly diverse array of green flexibility assets while ensuring our market-leading platform remains exceptionally stable and performant.

What is Optimisation in Flex?
The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns.

The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies.

The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute.

Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine.

🚀 What you’ll own:
The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). A Head of Engineering leading a Chapter is a senior leadership role combining strong product thinking, engineering judgement, operational awareness, and people leadership. They manage managers and senior individual contributors, helping teams own their product surfaces, make sound trade-offs, and deliver reliably.

This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. Ultimately, they maintain the technical vision for their specific area, ensuring services are appropriately owned, maintained, and aligned with Flex's sustainable growth.

  • Managing the leads.

  • The overall team architecture

  • Ensuring the services in that area are owned and maintained appropriately.

  • Ensuring that product features are built in a way that scales, is cost-effective, and is in line with the vision for a product area.

  • Ensuring the appropriate level of quality and resilience, with a specific focus on reducing system incidents and improving stability.

  • Ensuring appropriate tech debt is prioritised to support sustainable delivery.

  • Potentially managing a squad (team) as well.

You’ll be a strong fit if you have experience leading engineering teams across multiple squads, teams or product areas in a complex product environment.

Our end-to-end technology stack helps app marketers acquire and retain high-value users, while enabling publishers to maximize revenue across programmatic and direct demand.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Liftoff’s solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, Liftoff has a diverse, global presence.</span></p></div><p><strong>About the team:</strong></p> <p>As Senior Account Manager, you'll be a senior individual contributor and a cornerstone of our commercial team. title: Director/Senior Director, Molecular Discovery
description: <p><strong>Your Impact at LILA</strong></p> <p>The Director, Molecular Discovery is responsible for ensuring our autonomous science platform reliably and repeatedly delivers validated small-molecule drug candidates against designated targets at increasing speed. The platform generates and tests hypotheses at superhuman scale, and you ensure that process translates into real, high-quality compounds that advance toward the clinic.</p> <p>This role leans heavily into the AI and computational side of our workflow: you will be accountable for throughput, quality, and the operational health of the discovery engine, working hand-in-hand with AI scientists, computational chemists, and platform engineers to diagnose bottlenecks, close feedback loops, and continuously improve how the platform performs.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Be Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own small molecule discovery programs against assigned targets, from hit identification through lead optimization and candidate nomination.</li> <li>Serve as the accountable leader for discovery output setting and hitting timelines, quality benchmarks, and throughput targets across active programs.</li> <li>Operate as the primary interface between the autonomous science platform and drug discovery decision-making, ensuring that what the platform produces meets the bar for potency, selectivity, ADMET properties, and developability.</li> <li>Collaborate daily with AI/ML, robotics, and software engineering teams to close the loop between computational predictions and experimental results, driving continuous improvement of the platform's predictive accuracy and experimental efficiency.</li> <li>Architect the components of each discovery program end to end, specifying the required assays, building or sourcing the right capabilities, and managing the scientific staff needed to execute. Define and enforce the quality standards, assay cascades, and decision criteria that govern how compounds progress through the pipeline.</li> <li>Facilitate relationships with CROs and external partners for specialized studies (e.g., in vivo pharmacology, safety pharmacology, DMPK) that sit outside the automated platform.</li> <li>Provide drug discovery expertise to Lila's product team for commercial partnerships, translating platform capabilities into credible value propositions for pharma and biotech collaborators.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Need to Succeed</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ph.D. in medicinal chemistry, computational chemistry, chemical biology, or a closely related discipline.</li> <li>12+ years of experience in small molecule drug discovery from the computational, medicinal chemistry, or program leadership side with at least 5 years in a senior role closely involved in advancing compounds from hit-to-lead through candidate selection.</li> <li>Demonstrated involvement in programs that delivered clinical candidates, with enough proximity to compound progression decisions to own them whether from the computational, medicinal chemistry, or program leadership side.</li> <li>Deep fluency in medicinal chemistry principles, you may not have practiced bench medchem, but you understand SAR, synthetic tractability, and the multiparameter tradeoffs at the core of lead optimization (potency, selectivity, ADMET, PK, safety) well enough to guide them or define systematic decision frameworks for them.</li> <li>Operational mindset, experience running discovery programs with clear metrics, milestones, and accountability structures, and a comfort level with managing throughput and efficiency alongside scientific quality.</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of ADMET, DMPK, and the data packages required to advance a candidate to IND-enabling studies.</li> <li>Fluency with AI/ML-driven molecular design approaches (generative chemistry, molecular property prediction, free energy methods, active learning) and the practical judgment to know when computational output is actionable and when it needs experimental validation. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.</p> <p>We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.</p></div><p><strong>About this role</strong></p> <p>Faire’s quality, depth, and breadth of brands is its strongest value to retailers. stellar performer: someone who has finished top 3 in their org, qualified for President’s Club or All-Stars, and is hungry to do it again in a market that is genuinely early and genuinely exciting.</p> <p><strong>You’re excited about this opportunity because…</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have been top of the leaderboard before and you want to do it in the German-speaking market’s largest, receive orders and grow</li> </ul> <p><strong>Lead a best-in-class enterprise sales cycle</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead every customer interaction with a personalised, insight-led approach: understanding near-term activation with long-term platform success at enterprise scale</li> <li>Make independent, well-reasoned decisions on when to advance a deal and when to pass, and own the outcome either way</li> <li>Stay resilient and input-focused when performance is challenging; model the standard for the team</li> </ul> <p><strong>Be the expert on the DACH market</strong></p> <ul> <li>Be Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting.&nbsp;<br></span></em></p> <p><strong>Why you’ll love working at Faire</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Move fast:</strong> You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.</li> <li><strong>Equipped to scale:</strong> We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.</li> <li><strong>Best in class:</strong> Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.</li> <li><strong>Real rewards.</strong> Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.</li> <li><strong>Belonging:</strong> We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.</li> </ul> <p>Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. description: About Volta Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds. About The Role The Finance Business Partner will be embedded within the Project Controllership Organization, acting as the finance owner for large, long-duration capital projects from initial commitment through to completion and transfer to operations. You will bring rigorous project and cost accounting to the delivery teams: owning capex and cost accounting for your projects, building and maintaining project cost structures, tracking budgets, commitments and actuals, reporting variances with insight, and ensuring each project is accounted for accurately under US GAAP and closed out cleanly at completion. This is a hands-on role that pairs technical accounting depth with genuine business partnering - you will sit alongside project directors, engineers and procurement, not apart from them. What You Will Be Doing Project and capex accounting Capex accounting: own end-to-end accounting for assigned capital projects, including construction in progress (CIP/AUC), capitalization assessments under US GAAP (ASC 360), componentization, capitalized interest where applicable (ASC 835-20), and transfer to fixed assets on completion with correct in-service dates and useful lives. Compute and equipment capex: own the accounting for high-value compute and network equipment (GPU fleets and associated infrastructure), including vendor purchase order and financing payment tracking, delivery acceptance and in-service dating, componentization and useful lives, residual value support, and lessor accounting for intra-group equipment leases (ASC 842). Cost accounting: maintain accurate, complete and well-classified project cost records - distinguishing capital from operating expenditure, applying the capitalization policy consistently, and ensuring costs land in the correct entity, project, site and cost category. Project costing: build and own project cost breakdown structures (WBS/cost codes) aligned to contracts, procurement packages and the accounting dimension framework; establish cost baselines and estimates-at-completion (EAC) and keep them current. Accruals and commitments: run monthly cost accruals from contractor applications for payment, certifications and goods receipts; maintain the committed cost position (POs, contracts, change orders) and reconcile committed, accrued and actual spend. Month-end close: deliver project close activities to the group timetable - CIP reconciliations, accrual journals, retention and milestone payment tracking, and balance sheet substantiation for project-related accounts. Reporting, variance analysis and forecasting Variance reporting: produce monthly project cost reports comparing actuals and EAC against budget and prior forecast; explain variances with root-cause commentary and work with project teams on corrective actions. Forecasting: partner with FP&A and Strategic Finance on capex cashflow forecasting, phasing of spend, and funding drawdown planning for your projects. Provide current capex phasing and estimate-at-completion data into Strategic Finance's monthly business plan refresh. Board and investor reporting: contribute project cost and progress data to board packs, lender/investor reporting and management information, ensuring one version of the truth between delivery and finance. Work within, and help build, the group project reporting framework. Balance sheet visibility: own the project-related balance sheet - CIP, retentions, VAT recoverable, prepayments and committed spend - and feed these positions into the group management balance sheet dashboard on an automated, near-real-time basis. Project lifecycle and business partnering Cradle to completion: support projects through their full lifecycle - business case and budget setting, contract award, execution, change management, practical completion, final account settlement, and financial close-out including release of retentions and accrual true-ups. Change control: evaluate the cost and accounting impact of scope changes, change orders and claims; ensure changes are approved, coded and forecast before costs are incurred. Business partnering: act as the trusted finance counterpart to project directors, construction managers, procurement and engineering; challenge constructively, translate financial data into decisions, and embed cost discipline in delivery teams. Contract and procurement support: work with procurement and legal on the financial aspects of construction and equipment contracts (payment mechanisms, milestones, retentions, bonds, liquidated damages) and ensure compliance with the Group Procurement Policy and PO controls. Controls, policy and audit Controls: operate and help design internal controls over project costs, capitalization and payments as part of the group's SOX 404 readiness program, including preparing clear documentation and audit evidence. Policy: apply and help refine group accounting policies (capitalization, PP&E, procurement) and prepare technical accounting analysis for project-specific matters, escalating judgmental issues with well-structured recommendations. Audit: act as the primary project-accounting contact for external audit on assigned projects, preparing schedules, reconciliations and supporting evidence. Anything else that makes sense: as an early hire in a fast-scaling finance function, contribute to systems implementation (ERP selection ongoing), process design, and whatever else is needed to build best-in-class project controllership. raw.title: Finance Business Partner - Project Controllership
raw.description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

The Finance Business Partner will be embedded within the Project Controllership Organization, acting as the finance owner for large, long-duration capital projects from initial commitment through to completion and transfer to operations. You will bring rigorous project and cost accounting to the delivery teams: owning capex and cost accounting for your projects, building and maintaining project cost structures, tracking budgets, commitments and actuals, reporting variances with insight, and ensuring each project is accounted for accurately under US GAAP and closed out cleanly at completion. This is a hands-on role that pairs technical accounting depth with genuine business partnering - you will sit alongside project directors, engineers and procurement, not apart from them.

What You Will Be Doing

Project and capex accounting

  • Capex accounting: own end-to-end accounting for assigned capital projects, including construction in progress (CIP/AUC), capitalization assessments under US GAAP (ASC 360), componentization, capitalized interest where applicable (ASC 835-20), and transfer to fixed assets on completion with correct in-service dates and useful lives.

  • Compute and equipment capex: own the accounting for high-value compute and network equipment (GPU fleets and associated infrastructure), including vendor purchase order and financing payment tracking, delivery acceptance and in-service dating, componentization and useful lives, residual value support, and lessor accounting for intra-group equipment leases (ASC 842).

  • Cost accounting: maintain accurate, complete and well-classified project cost records - distinguishing capital from operating expenditure, applying the capitalization policy consistently, and ensuring costs land in the correct entity, project, site and cost category.

  • Project costing: build and own project cost breakdown structures (WBS/cost codes) aligned to contracts, procurement packages and the accounting dimension framework; establish cost baselines and estimates-at-completion (EAC) and keep them current.

  • Accruals and commitments: run monthly cost accruals from contractor applications for payment, certifications and goods receipts; maintain the committed cost position (POs, contracts, change orders) and reconcile committed, accrued and actual spend.

  • Month-end close: deliver project close activities to the group timetable - CIP reconciliations, accrual journals, retention and milestone payment tracking, and balance sheet substantiation for project-related accounts.

Reporting, variance analysis and forecasting

  • Variance reporting: produce monthly project cost reports comparing actuals and EAC against budget and prior forecast; explain variances with root-cause commentary and work with project teams on corrective actions.

  • Forecasting: partner with FP&A and Strategic Finance on capex cashflow forecasting, phasing of spend, and funding drawdown planning for your projects. Provide current capex phasing and estimate-at-completion data into Strategic Finance's monthly business plan refresh.

  • Board and investor reporting: contribute project cost and progress data to board packs, lender/investor reporting and management information, ensuring one version of the truth between delivery and finance. Work within, and help build, the group project reporting framework.

  • Balance sheet visibility: own the project-related balance sheet - CIP, retentions, VAT recoverable, prepayments and committed spend - and feed these positions into the group management balance sheet dashboard on an automated, near-real-time basis.

Project lifecycle and business partnering

  • Cradle to completion: support projects through their full lifecycle - business case and budget setting, contract award, execution, change management, practical completion, final account settlement, and financial close-out including release of retentions and accrual true-ups.

  • Change control: evaluate the cost and accounting impact of scope changes, change orders and claims; ensure changes are approved, coded and forecast before costs are incurred.

  • Business partnering: act as the trusted finance counterpart to project directors, construction managers, procurement and engineering; challenge constructively, translate financial data into decisions, and embed cost discipline in delivery teams.

  • Contract and procurement support: work with procurement and legal on the financial aspects of construction and equipment contracts (payment mechanisms, milestones, retentions, bonds, liquidated damages) and ensure compliance with the Group Procurement Policy and PO controls.

Controls, policy and audit

  • Controls: operate and help design internal controls over project costs, capitalization and payments as part of the group's SOX 404 readiness program, including preparing clear documentation and audit evidence.

  • Policy: apply and help refine group accounting policies (capitalization, PP&E, procurement) and prepare technical accounting analysis for project-specific matters, escalating judgmental issues with well-structured recommendations.

  • Audit: act as the primary project-accounting contact for external audit on assigned projects, preparing schedules, reconciliations and supporting evidence.

  • Anything else that makes sense: as an early hire in a fast-scaling finance function, contribute to systems implementation (ERP selection ongoing), process design, and whatever else is needed to build best-in-class project controllership.

What You Bring

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent) with strong post-qualification experience.

  • Demonstrable experience of project accounting for large, long-term capital projects - for example data centers, energy, utilities, infrastructure, construction or industrial facilities - covering the full project lifecycle.

  • Deep, practical knowledge of capex and cost accounting: CIP/AUC, capitalization criteria, componentization, accruals from contractor valuations, retentions, and asset transfer at completion.

  • Experience building and managing project cost structures (WBS/cost coding), budgets, committed cost tracking and estimates-at-completion.

  • Strong variance analysis and reporting skills, with the ability to explain cost movements clearly to non-finance stakeholders.

  • Proven business partnering experience embedded with, or working closely alongside, project delivery teams.

  • Advanced Excel and strong data and dashboarding skills, with an automation-first mindset; comfortable working from imperfect data in a scaling environment.

Nice To Have

  • US GAAP experience (ASC 360 fixed assets, ASC 835-20 capitalized interest, ASC 842 leases as they touch project sites).

  • Experience in a SOX-regulated or IPO-readiness environment, or supporting external audits of major capital projects.

  • Exposure to multi-entity, multi-currency structures and cross-border projects.

  • Nordic experience - local statutory reporting alongside US GAAP, and VAT on construction and imports.

  • Experience accounting for high-value technology or compute equipment (GPU, network or telecoms assets), including intra-group equipment leasing.

  • Familiarity with project controls disciplines (cost engineering, earned value, contract administration) and construction contract forms.

  • Experience of ERP and project accounting systems implementation.

Lead Product Designer

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)

💰 £70k-£90k (negotiable)

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group

  • Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

  • Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

  • Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

  • Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

  • You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

  • You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

  • You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

  • You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

  • You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

  • You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

  • You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

  • You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you

  • Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

  • Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

  • AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

  • Craft: Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach. You have views on interaction quality, hierarchy, motion, microcopy - and you can defend them.

  • Cross-functional: Comfortable as a peer at the table with product and engineering counterparts in your domain. Drive direction; don't wait for it.

  • Open to flex: This is predominantly an IC role, but we're not rigid about it. If you've line-managed before, or want to take on one or two direct reports alongside the IC work, we're open to that conversation.

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

Job Title: Staff Product Designer
Location: London, Hybrid (3 days in office)
Portfolio: A link to your portfolio is required and must be included on your CV or within your application.

About Gen:

We're not just a company; we're a global force. Fiercely committed to ensuring that everyone, everywhere, can live their lives digitally safe. Our family of brands, Norton, Avast, LifeLock, Avira, AVG, ReputationDefender and CCleaner, unite the brightest minds, the sharpest tech and the most diverse thinking to protect over 500 million people. And we've built an inclusive workplace, where your well-being is a priority because true success comes from a place of balance and authenticity. When you're thriving, you're unstoppable. So, bring us your bold ideas and passion that refuses to quit. The digital world isn't some distant reality, it's the world we live in, and we're ready for it. If you're ready to push boundaries and be part of something bigger, join #TeamGen.

How We Work:

Our hybrid work style (3 days in the London office) gives us the face-to-face time to have creative conversations, meaningful meetings, make quick decisions and build relationships. And it's flexible enough to give you the space to do your best work.

About the Role:

We're reimagining how people connect with and protect what matters most. This role has a key focus on Avast's freemium experiences, one of Gen's largest consumer software products with hundreds of millions of users globally across desktop and mobile. As part of a global company known for brands like Norton, LifeLock, MoneyLion and Avast, we're building new products and experiences that address real-world challenges with clarity, purpose and empathy.

We're also on a mission to become an AI-first company, infusing intelligent systems, automation and personalisation into everything we do. From how we design user experiences to how we protect identities and enable secure financial wellness, AI is central to our strategy, and design plays a key role in making it accessible, trustworthy and human.

This is an opportunity to join an established yet entrepreneurial environment, where your craft is valued, your impact is felt, and your ideas help shape the future of digital security and secure financial wellness.

About the Team:

Gen's Global Product Design team is a diverse, distributed group working across London, Prague, Dublin and the US. The global team designs across cybersecurity, identity protection, privacy and financial wellness, with a strong focus on AI-enabled experiences and reimagining key user journeys. This role sits within the cyber safety pillar, working primarily on Avast and its freemium ecosystem, while staying closely connected to the wider design community across Gen's brands.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Shape strategy through design: translate complex problems and abstract ideas into elegant, usable solutions grounded in user needs and business goals

  • Design intelligent experiences: bring clarity and usability to AI-powered products by designing interactions that feel natural, transparent and trustworthy

  • Turn insights into impact: translate complex problems and abstract ideas into simple, usable and delightful solutions grounded in user needs and data

  • Prototype and test with AI: explore new possibilities through discovery, rapid prototyping and user testing, especially around how AI can simplify tasks or personalise experiences

  • Collaborate and influence: partner across disciplines to align design outcomes with user needs, business goals and AI capabilities

  • Champion design quality: ensure every touchpoint, whether powered by AI or not, is cohesive, accessible and human-centred

About You:

Education: degree in Design, HCI or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

Experience:

  • A track record of designing and shipping mobile-first B2C products at scale, ideally in industries like security, fintech, health or adjacent spaces

  • Comfortable operating across time zones and cultures; experience with distributed teams is a plus

  • Experience designing for or alongside AI-driven features such as personalisation, recommendations or automation is a strong plus

  • Experience in cybersecurity or financial services is helpful, but curiosity and adaptability matter more

Skills:

  • Strategic mindset with a keen sense of how design drives user value and business growth

  • Mastery of end-to-end product design: UX research, interaction, visual design and systems thinking

  • Deep user empathy and a belief in data-informed design decisions

Personal Attributes:

  • Curious, adaptable and motivated by solving complex problems for real people at scale

  • A clear, compelling portfolio that demonstrates your design process and product impact

Benefits:

At Gen Digital, we are committed to supporting our employees' well-being and professional growth. Our comprehensive benefits package for UK team members includes:

  • Health & Wellbeing: company-paid private medical insurance, dental and vision benefits, plus access to mental health and wellbeing support through our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)

  • Financial Security: a Group Personal Pension Plan with auto-enrolment for eligible employees, together with the opportunity to purchase Gen stock through our Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

  • Unlimited Paid Time Off: available once statutory annual leave has been used, plus company holidays and a range of leave options to support personal and family needs

  • Tuition Reimbursement: up to £5,150 per calendar year for job-related accredited courses that support career development within Gen

  • Wellness Reimbursement: up to $450 per year to cover fitness-related expenses

  • Sustainability Allowance: a $500 annual sustainable home improvement allowance

  • Additional Perks: access to adoption assistance, family support services, legal assistance plans and exclusive employee discounts

What's Next:

Your CV and portfolio (please make sure a link to your portfolio is included on your CV or within your application) will be reviewed by the recruiter and hiring manager to understand the scope of your work, the impact you've delivered, and how your experience aligns with the role.

If shortlisted, the recruiter will be in touch to set up a conversation to learn more about your background, what's motivating you, why you're interested in Gen and our products, and to go through the interview process.

Gen is an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to fair, inclusive practices at every stage of the candidate and employee journey. Employment decisions are based on merit, experience and business needs.
