title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement. Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply. What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator. What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Conditions Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

description: <div class="content-intro"><div style="font-family: 'Instrument Sans', 'Segoe UI', Trebuchet MS, Tahoma, sans-serif;"> <p style="line-height: 1.4;">Vast is developing next-generation <strong>space stations and space infrastructure</strong> using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced <strong>Vast Satellite</strong>, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.</p> <p style="line-height: 1.4;">Headquartered in<strong> Long Beach, California</strong>, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.</p> </div></div><p>Vast recherche un(e) <strong>Directeur(trice), Développement Commercial International - Satellites</strong>, sous la responsabilité du <strong>SVP, Satellite Business Development &amp; Commercialization</strong>, pour diriger le développement commercial axé sur le commerce (communications, observation de la Terre, détection, défense et applications de calcul en orbite) et les gouvernements internationaux pour Vast Satellites. Ce rôle est centré sur les marchés hors États-Unis — notamment l'Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l'Asie — et dirigera l'engagement client, le développement des opportunités, la stratégie de capture, l'engagement gouvernemental/défense et les efforts de partenariat qui font progresser les initiatives de Vast pour développer, fabriquer et exploiter des plateformes de bus satellites avancées.</p> <p>Il s'agit d'une petite équipe commerciale fondatrice de haut niveau : le rôle exige à la fois des instincts de « hunter » en développement commercial (créer des marchés et de la demande là où il n'en existe pas encore) et des compétences avérées de « closer » (négocier et exécuter des contrats allant de quelques millions à des centaines de millions de dollars).</p> <p>Ce poste sera à <strong>temps plein, exempté</strong>, ouvert à un lieu de travail international flexible comme décrit ci-dessus.</p> <p><strong>Responsabilités :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Élaborer et exécuter une stratégie globale de marché commercial et gouvernemental international couvrant l'Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l'Asie, alignée sur les objectifs commerciaux de Vast.</li> <li>Établir et maintenir une veille stratégique sur le marché et la concurrence concernant les clients spatiaux commerciaux et gouvernementaux internationaux, en distinguant le positionnement de Vast de celui de ses concurrents dans chaque région.</li> <li>Piloter la planification interne pour la priorisation des opportunités internationales, la stratégie de capture et le développement du pipeline sur de multiples marchés alliés et partenaires.</li> <li>Diriger l'engagement client à travers l'identification d'opportunités, la définition du périmètre des missions, les présentations de capacités et le développement de concepts précoces avec les opérateurs commerciaux internationaux, les sociétés d'observation de la Terre, les ministères de la défense et les entités gouvernementales.</li> <li>Tirer parti d'un solide réseau préexistant de haut niveau au sein de la chaîne de valeur internationale de l'espace et de la défense pour ouvrir des portes auprès de clients potentiels et identifier précocement les menaces concurrentielles.</li> <li>Diriger l'élaboration des propositions et coordonner les contributions interfonctionnelles des équipes d'ingénierie, de gestion de programme, de finance, juridique et de contrôle des exportations/conformité, avec le soutien de l'analyste BD et de l'ingénieur avant-vente de l'équipe.</li> <li>Assumer la responsabilité du développement du pipeline, des prévisions et des rapports pour tous les comptes commerciaux et gouvernementaux internationaux.</li> <li>Négocier et conclure des contrats pour des missions commerciales et gouvernementales/défense internationales et les services associés, en naviguant à travers divers cadres nationaux de passation de marchés, de contrôle des exportations (ex. ITAR/EAR) et de partenariat.</li> <li>Se coordonner avec l'équipe de sécurité nationale de Vast lorsque les programmes internationaux croisent des parties prenantes ou des enjeux liés au gouvernement américain.</li> <li>Représenter Vast lors d'événements de l'industrie spatiale, aérospatiale et de défense internationale en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Asie.</li> <li>Faire des présentations, participer à des panels et fournir des briefings de haut niveau/C-suite communiquant les capacités et la valeur des plateformes satellites de Vast aux audiences commerciales, gouvernementales et de défense internationales.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Qualifications Minimales :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Plus de 12 ans d'expérience pertinente dans le développement commercial spatial/aérospatial, les ventes, la gestion de capture ou les contrats gouvernementaux/défense, avec un succès avéré en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et/ou en Asie.</li> <li>Historique avéré d'origination et de conclusion personnelle de contrats, y compris des transactions de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars ou plus.</li> <li>Relations établies et vérifiables avec des clients potentiels au niveau cadre et exécutif, et connaissance du paysage concurrentiel sur de multiples marchés spatiaux et de défense internationaux.</li> <li>Expérience dans la chaîne de valeur spatiale/aérospatiale (lancement, bus satellite, charge utile, intégration maître d'œuvre ou opérations), idéalement complémentaire des opérations satellites — par ex. observation de la Terre ou défense internationale.</li> <li>Compréhension approfondie des structures de passation de marchés et de partenariat gouvernementales internationales pertinentes pour les programmes d'espace et de défense.</li> <li>Solides compétences techniques et capacité à communiquer des systèmes complexes à des audiences commerciales, de défense et gouvernementales internationales.</li> <li>Excellentes capacités de communication, d'analyse, de collaboration et de relations interpersonnelles ; à l'aise pour opérer à travers diverses cultures et langues.</li> <li>Capacité à opérer de manière autonome, à hiérarchiser les priorités efficacement et à gérer simultanément plusieurs projets internationaux dans un environnement de petite équipe au rythme soutenu.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Compétences et Expériences Souhaitées :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Relations et crédibilité établies en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Asie.</li> <li>Maîtrise des langues pertinentes pour les marchés cibles (français, arabe, japonais, etc.).</li> <li>Expérience de travail aux côtés d'équipes d'affaires publiques locales ou coordination avec celles-ci (ex. affaires publiques gouvernementales françaises/UE).</li> <li>Connaissance des régimes de contrôle des exportations (ITAR/EAR) dans les programmes de satellites internationaux.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Exigences Supplémentaires :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Capacité à voyager plus de 50 % du temps.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <hr> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Vast is looking for a&nbsp;<strong>Director, Satellite Business Development International</strong>, reporting to the <strong>SVP, Satellite Business Development &amp; Commercialization</strong>, to lead commercial (communications, Earth observation, sensing, defense, and in-orbit compute applications) and international government-focused business development for Vast Satellites. This role is focused on markets outside the United States — including Europe, the Middle East, and Asia — and will lead customer engagement, opportunity development, capture strategy, government/defense engagement, and partnership efforts that advance Vast's initiatives to develop, manufacture, and operate advanced satellite bus platforms.</p> <p>This is a small, senior founding commercial team: the role demands both business development "hunter" instincts (creating markets and demand where none exist yet) and proven "closer" skills (negotiating and executing contracts from single-digit millions to hundreds of millions of dollars).&nbsp;</p> <p>This will be a <strong>full-time, exempt</strong> position open to a flexible international location as described above.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and execute a comprehensive international commercial and government market strategy spanning Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, aligned with Vast's business objectives.</li> <li>Build and maintain a market and competitive intelligence view across international commercial and government space customers, distinguishing Vast's positioning from competitors in each region.</li> <li>Lead internal planning for international opportunity prioritization, capture strategy, and pipeline development across multiple allied and partner markets.</li> <li>Lead customer engagement across opportunity identification, mission scoping, capability briefings, and early concept development with international commercial operators, Earth observation companies, defense ministries, and government entities.</li> <li>Leverage a strong, pre-existing senior-level network across the international space/defense value chain to open doors with potential customers and identify competitive threats early.</li> <li>Lead proposal development and coordinate cross-functional contributions from engineering, program management, finance, legal, and export-control/compliance teams, supported by the team's BD analyst and pre-sales engineer.</li> <li>Own pipeline development, forecasting, and reporting across all international commercial and government accounts.</li> <li>Negotiate and close contracts for international commercial and government/defense missions and associated services, navigating varying national procurement, export-control (e.g., ITAR/EAR), and partnership frameworks.</li> <li>Coordinate with Vast's National Security team where international programs intersect with US Government stakeholders or content.</li> <li>Represent Vast at international space, aerospace, and defense industry events across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.</li> <li>Deliver presentations, participate in panels, and provide senior/C-suite-level briefings that communicate the capabilities and value of Vast's satellite platforms to international commercial, government, and defense audiences.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Minimum Qualifications:</strong></p> <ul> <li>12+ years of relevant experience in space/aerospace business development, sales, capture management, or government/defense contracting, with demonstrated success operating in Europe, the Middle East, and/or Asia.</li> <li>Proven track record of personally originating and closing contracts, including deals in the tens of millions of dollars or above.</li> <li>Established, verifiable senior and executive-level relationships with potential customers, and knowledge of the competitive landscape across multiple international space/defense markets.</li> <li>Background in the space/aerospace value chain (launch, satellite bus, payload, prime integration, or operations), ideally complementary to satellite operations — e.g., Earth observation or international defense.</li> <li>Deep understanding of international government procurement and partnership structures relevant to space and defense programs.</li> <li>Strong technical understanding and ability to communicate complex systems to international commercial, defense, and government audiences.</li> <li>Excellent communication, analytical, collaboration, and interpersonal skills; comfortable operating across cultures and languages.</li> <li>Ability to operate independently, prioritize effectively, and manage multiple international efforts simultaneously in a fast-paced, lean-team environment.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Skills &amp; Experience:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Existing relationships and credibility across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.</li> <li>Fluency in languages relevant to target markets (French, Arabic, Japanese, etc.).</li> <li>Experience working alongside or coordinating with in-country government affairs teams (e.g., French/EU government affairs).</li> <li>Familiarity with export-control regimes (ITAR/EAR) in international satellite programs.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Additional Requirements:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel 50%+ of the time.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><div style="font-family: 'Instrument Sans', 'Segoe UI', Trebuchet MS, Tahoma, sans-serif;"> <p style="line-height: 1; font-size: 14px;"><em>We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.</em></p> <p style="line-height: 1;">&nbsp;</p> <p style="line-height: 1;"><strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS<br></strong><br>Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee &amp; onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees.</p> <p style="line-height: 1;"><strong><br>U.S. EXPORT CONTROL COMPLIANCE STATUS<br><br></strong>The person hired will have access to information and items subject to U.S. export controls, and therefore, must either be a “U.S. person” as defined by&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22/section-120.62">22 C.F.R. § 120.62</a> or otherwise eligible for deemed export licensing. description: Role: Senior Product Designer Company: SimpleStudy Location: Remote, Europe (preferably Western / continental); relocation to Lisbon possible Job Type: Full-time About SimpleStudy SimpleStudy is an AI exam prep platform that students find and choose for themselves. In some numbers: 1.5M+ students across the UK, Ireland, Brazil, South Africa, and Australia 40–50k new students every week Web, mobile, and desktop apps $4M seed round with investors from Strava, OpenAI, and Meta The traction came fast. Now the company is refounding: rebuilding the brand, the design language, and the product experience from scratch. The product grew like a Jenga tower, one feature on top of another. The job now is to rebuild it as a pyramid. The team is ~30 people, remote with a Lisbon office — lean, product-led, and deliberately not a typical edtech company. You'll report to José, the Founding Designer, and work with him as a partner. José tends to lead early framing and direction. You bring strong craft and take the work to the finish line, in close sync with engineering. You both shape the new design language, and you push back with a better idea when you see one. What you are expected to do: Shape the new design language and brand: design system, rebrand, and the new mobile app. Own the full design process — from an ambiguous problem to a polished, shipped solution. Drive the consumer experience: onboarding, social features, retention, and the learning loop. Work in close sync with engineers and PM, not as a handoff step - polish the implementation together until it feels right. Bring your own initiatives and say "no, but…" when you see a better way. Raise the bar for the whole design team. What you need to succeed: High craft — your visual work is polished and intentional; the details reveal your thinking. Storytelling over process — you take an ambiguous problem, frame it, and make it simple. Your portfolio shows artifacts, not diagrams; it has a point of view. Consumer instinct — you've shipped B2C products that people chose to use. You understand product metrics and use them as input, but you lead with feel and craft. Opinions with backbone — you have a design philosophy, can defend it under pushback, and bring your own initiatives. You don't wait to be told what to build. Energy and curiosity — you're an interesting person with a life outside work, and you leave people energised after a conversation. English — fluent, written and spoken. Position description
 
At Sonar, we believe that simply reporting code issues is not sufficient. To truly level up the quality of the world's software, we must empower millions of developers to fix them automatically. With over 400,000 enterprises relying on our products, we hold a unique lever to shape how software is built.
 
Recent breakthroughs in AI have made autonomous remediation a reality, but one major hurdle remains: Trust. Generative AI makes mistakes, and enterprises cannot automate what they do not trust. This is where you come in. As a Senior/Staff Engineer, you will architect the backend for Verified Autonomous Remediation, a sophisticated Agentic workflow that doesn’t just generate code, but rigorously tests and validates it using Sonar’s analysis engine. You will tackle the hard engineering problems required to close the "Trust Gap."

What you will do
  • Architect the "Unified Remediation Engine". You will design the high-throughput decision logic that powers our remediation efforts. You will build the backend services that intelligently route requests between deterministic instant QuickFixes, LLM-based reasoning fixes, and complex Agentic flows.
  • Build Robust Agent Architecture. You will contribute to the Sonar Remediation Agent code, transitioning research concepts to a resilient, high-scale production service. You will implement self-healing workflows where the Agent iteratively fixes the code it produces until the build is green.
  • Solve the "Sandboxing" Problem. You will architect the secure execution environments required to run untrusted, AI-generated code. You will design the isolation layers that allow Agents to iterate on code improvements without compromising our infrastructure.
  • Engineer for Reliability & Safety. You will implement critical safety mechanisms, like Circuit Breakers to automatically reroute requests to the proper engine when acceptance rates drop. Crucially, you will own the cost/performance trade-off, ensuring our AWS architecture scales to millions of events without letting token costs spiral.
  • Act as a Technical "Force Multiplier". Beyond building systems, you’ll mentor the squad through design reviews and collaborate with the Research team to ensure our agent is not just state-of-the-art, but production-safe.

    • Experience and qualifications
  • Strong Backend & Cloud Expertise. You have 8+ years of experience building scalable resilient systems. You are strong in AWS architecture and know how to design for high availability and low latency with cost in mind.
  • Polyglot Ecosystem (Java & Python). You are comfortable operating in a hybrid environment: Java for deep integration with the Core Sonar analysis engine and Python for the AI/Agent reasoning layer. You should be strong in one and capable in the other. We make use of various LLM tools, and are looking for people not afraid of different languages.
  • Systems Thinking. You understand that "AI" in production is mostly "Systems Engineering." You know how to handle asynchronous event-driven architectures, manage queues, and design sandboxed execution environments to run untrusted code safely.
  • AI & LLM Integration. You have practical experience building applications that orchestrate LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or hosted open models). You understand the backend complexity of RAG, context window management, and prompt engineering at scale.
  • Data-Driven Mindset. You care about the "Why." You want to build telemetry pipelines that distinguish between "Bad UX" and "Bad Code," focusing on the metrics that matter.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. This is not SaaS slop, you're making physical machines do precise biology with minimal human intervention. What we're looking for Strong experience designing and building production backend systems. You'll be handling large volumes of heterogeneous data from physical instruments such as binding kinetics data, enzyme activity measurements, chromatography readings, and turning them into clean, structured datasets. A genuine interest in biology. No background required, but our product is running biology experiments in the physical world and that should excite you. High-autonomy, founder mindset. We share context and vision openly. You figure out what matters most and go work on it. Pragmatism. You care about solving the problem well, not about the stack or the tools. You write code primarily with AI, but you have enough experience writing software without it to know what good code and good architecture look like. description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role You are here to scale up data generation. Design teams can hand us 10⁶ sequences, and our automated infrastructure measures on the order of 10³ of them individually. Library construction and display is what closes that gap. We want someone who has set these systems up before and can do it again here, with their own hands. Phage, ribosome, mRNA, yeast, cell-free: which one fits depends on the library and the target, and part of the job is making that call and then building it rather than writing a recommendation. This is a build role, not a service role. For your first months you are making libraries, running selections, working out why a round collapsed, and turning what works into something the automation team can run without you. What You'll Do Build the libraries. Oligo pools, combinatorial assembly, barcoding. More campaigns fail here than at selection. Run selections end to end , including the call on whether a round enriched real binders or just fast growers. Pick the platform per campaign and stand it up. Based on the library and the target, not on what you happened to use last. Own the sequencing analysis. You don't need to be a bioinformatician, but you can't be waiting on one. Hand off to automation. A protocol that only works when you personally run it isn't finished. Close the loop. Selected designs get expressed and measured on BLI and SPR by the team next door. That tells you whether the selection worked. What We're Looking For MSc or PhD in a relevant field, plus 3+ years running display and selection yourself. You have set up a display platform, not just used one. This is the core requirement. Built the library, got the selection working, and produced binders that held up in an independent assay. Managing outsourced CRO campaigns is not the same thing. Depth in at least one display format and working literacy across the rest. We are not fixed on which one. High-diversity cloning , and an understanding of where bias enters a pool and what it costs you later. NGS as a routine tool , and FACS if you have it. Enough Python or R to analyze your own data without joining a queue. You use AI tools seriously. It's 2026 and we run on Claude Code across the company. You also need the judgment to check what comes back. A self-starter. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue. You decide what to build, build it, and tell us what you learned. Startup speed, not academic pace. Campaigns run against customer deadlines. A working platform with known limits beats an elegant one next year. You want your protocols automated rather than manual forever. If your instinct is that a campaign is finished once you have ten good clones, we will frustrate each other. We want data, not a hit list. Why This Role Is Interesting Most display scientists spend a career panning one target class, and the output is a hit list. Here you would run campaigns across many targets and many design methods, much of it on AI-designed proteins nobody has characterized before. Expression and characterization already run at scale on our automated infrastructure, so you build the selection layer and not everything underneath it. Details Location: Lausanne, Switzerland, on-site. This is a lab role. Type: Full time. Start date: As soon as you can. Application deadline We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.
